title: (RHBA-2007:0573) xorg-x11-server bug fix update
portal_summary: Updated xorg-x11-server packages that fix several bugs are now available.

portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure that all previously-released
errata relevant to your system have been applied.  

This update is available via Red Hat Network.  Details on how to use 
the Red Hat Network to apply this update are available at
http://kbase.redhat.com/faq/FAQ_58_10188
portal_description:
X.org X11 is an open source implementation of the X Window System. It
provides the basic low level functionality which full fledged graphical
user interfaces (GUIs) such as GNOME and KDE are designed upon.

These updated packages fix the following bugs:

* GLX textures were displayed incorrectly when desktop effects were
enabled. This bug affects the Apple iBook G3 and G4, but also affects other
machines using big-endian addressing.

* during a Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 installation anaconda reported that
X could not start. This issue occurred on the IBM System x3950, HP
Integrity Superdome SX1000, and SX2000 servers. Note: this list is not
exhaustive, other PCI chipsets on Itanium architectures could be affected.

* X failed to initialize on systems with large (more than 128 devices)
PCI configurations. NovaScale systems, among others, were affected.

* the NVIDIA VBIOS BSF and BSR instructions failed to be emulated
correctly. This effected the operation of the vesa driver on NVIDIA GPUs.
The NVIDIA G70 and G80 chips were particularly affected.

* using software GLX rendering with the X Display Manager Control Protocol
(XDMCP) caused the X server to crash during logout and shutdown.

* the following errors were reported in the X log file:

(WW) No monitor specified for screen "Screen0".
(WW) The core pointer device wasn't specified explicitly in the layout.
(WW) No FontPath specified.  Using compiled-in default.
(WW) <default pointer>: No Device specified, looking for one...
(EE) AIGLX: Screen 0 is not DRI capable

These warnings were for harmless conditions, and have been resolved in
these updated packages.

* OpenOffice hanged when attempting to open a drop-down menu, such as the
File menu.

* enabling acpi hotkeys caused X to crash when acpid generated an acpi
event, such as closing the lid on a laptop computer.

* in previous packages X failed to start when the "driver" value was set to
"radeon" in xorg.conf, when using the ATI ES1000 GPU chip. Setting the
"driver" value to "vesa" allowed X to start, but mouse movement caused X
to crash.

All xorg-x11-server users should upgrade to these updated packages, which
resolve these issues.
